docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.AuraBufferDesc.summary: Struct AuraBufferDesc Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Describes a buffer resource, including its size, usage, and other properties that control how the buffer is created and used in graphics applications. public struct AuraBufferDesc Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Constructors AuraBufferDesc() Initializes a new instance of the BufferDesc class. public AuraBufferDesc() AuraBufferDesc(ulong, BufferBindUsage, bool) Initializes a new instance of the BufferDesc class with the specified size, binding usage, and dynamic allocation option. public AuraBufferDesc(ulong sizeInBytes, BufferBindUsage usage = BufferBindUsage.VertexBuffer, bool dynamic = true) Parameters sizeInBytes ulong The size, in bytes, of the buffer to be described. Must be greater than zero. usage BufferBindUsage The intended binding usage for the buffer, such as vertex or index buffer. Defaults to VertexBuffer if not specified. dynamic bool A value indicating whether the buffer is intended for dynamic updates. Set to true for buffers that will be updated frequently; otherwise, false. Fields BindUsage The usage of the buffer, what will the buffer be used for? public BufferBindUsage BindUsage Field Value BufferBindUsage CpuReadback Should almost always be false. Allows the cpu to gather data out of a buffer. public bool CpuReadback Field Value bool EnableGrowth If true, the buffer can grow in size if needed. This is useful for dynamic buffers that may need to accommodate varying amounts of data over time. When enabled, the buffer can automatically resize itself. Always call bind after uploading data when using this option, as resizing consists of creating a new buffer and copying the old data to it, which will unbind the buffer. public bool EnableGrowth Field Value bool IsDynamic If true, this buffer will be considered dynamic, aka its data is going to be written once and read once before changing again. This allows the buffer to be optimized for this usage pattern, which can improve performance in certain scenarios, such as when frequently updating vertex data or other resources that require frequent modifications. Set this to false if the buffer is not going to be updated frequently, as it may allow for better performance in scenarios where the buffer data is static or infrequently modified. public bool IsDynamic Field Value bool SizeInBytes The size of the buffer in bytes. public ulong SizeInBytes Field Value ulong StructureStrideBytes For unordered access views, size of one of the structure in bytes. 0 means raw bytes, good luck buddy. For non UAV scenarios, leave at 0. public uint StructureStrideBytes Field Value uint

NUByte4 = 13 A vector of four normalized unsigned 8-bit integers. Per component range: 0.0f to 1.0f. NUShort = 19 A normalized unsigned 16-bit integer. Stored as ushort, interpreted as a float between 0.0f and 1.0f. NUShort2 = 24 A vector of two normalized unsigned 16-bit integers. Per component range: 0.0f to 1.0f. NUShort4 = 28 A vector of four normalized unsigned 16-bit integers. Per component range: 0.0f to 1.0f. SByte = 8 A signed 8-bit integer (sbyte). Range: -128 to 127. SByte2 = 9 A vector of two signed 8-bit integers. Range per component: -128 to 127. SByte4 = 10 A vector of four signed 8-bit integers. Range per component: -128 to 127. SShort = 18 A signed 16-bit integer (short). Range: -32,768 to 32,767. SShort2 = 21 A vector of two signed 16-bit integers. Per component range: -32,768 to 32,767. UByte2 = 6 A vector of two unsigned 8-bit integers. Range per component: 0 to 255. UByte4 = 7 A vector of four unsigned 8-bit integers. Range per component: 0 to 255. UInt = 33 An unsigned 32-bit integer (uint). Range: 0 to 4,294,967,295. UInt2 = 34 A vector of two unsigned 32-bit integers. Per component range: 0 to 2^32-1. UInt3 = 35 A vector of three unsigned 32-bit integers. Per component range: 0 to 2^32-1. UInt4 = 36 A vector of four unsigned 32-bit integers. Per component range: 0 to 2^32-1. UShort = 17 An unsigned 16-bit integer (ushort). Range: 0 to 65,535. UShort2 = 22 A vector of two unsigned 16-bit integers. Per component range: 0 to 65,535. UShort4 = 26 A vector of four unsigned 16-bit integers. Per component range: 0 to 65,535. Unknown = 37 An unknown or undefined format type. docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.IRenderTarget..summary: Class IRenderTarget Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Represents a render target resource instance, which is a texture that can be rendered to during rendering operations. A render target allows you to draw graphics onto a texture, enabling techniques such as off-screen rendering, post-processing effects, and dynamic texture generation. public class IRenderTarget : AuraResourcePointer, IDisposable Inheritance object AuraResourcePointer IRenderTarget Implements IDisposable Inherited Members AuraResourcePointer.Dispose() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties Description Retrieves the current render target description, including properties such as width, height, color format, MSAA settings, and clear color. public RenderTargetDesc Description { get; } Property Value RenderTargetDesc The description used to make this render target. Format Gets the color format of the render target texture. public AuraColorFormat Format { get; } Property Value AuraColorFormat FrameBufferIndex Gets the frame buffer index associated with this render target, which is optional but should map to a swapchain buffer index when applicable. Not sure why you'd need it in this case, but it's there if you need it. public uint FrameBufferIndex { get; } Property Value uint Height The height of the render target texture in pixels. public uint Height { get; } Property Value uint Heightf Gets the height of the render target texture in pixels as a float. public float Heightf { get; } Property Value float MsaaDescription Gets the MSAA description of the render target, which includes the sample count and quality level used for multisample anti-aliasing. This information is important for understanding the anti-aliasing capabilities of the render target and how it will affect rendering quality and performance. Lets you get just that without having to get the entire description if you only care about the MSAA settings. Note that the MSAA settings are also included in the full description, so you can get them from there as well if you need other information at the same time. public MsaaDesc MsaaDescription { get; } Property Value MsaaDesc The multisampling anti aliasing description. Size Gets the size of the render target texture as a vector (width, height). public Vec2I Size { get; } Property Value Vec2I Sizef Gets the size of the render target texture as a vector (width, height) as floats. public Vec2 Sizef { get; } Property Value Vec2 Texture Gets the texture associated with this render target, which can be used for binding or other operations like updating or reading back. public ITexture Texture { get; } Property Value ITexture Width The width of the render target texture in pixels. public uint Width { get; } Property Value uint Widthf Gets the width of the render target texture in pixels as a float. public float Widthf { get; } Property Value float Methods Bind(int) Binds the texture to a slot for rendering. This makes the render target's texture available for use in shader resource bindings, allowing it to be sampled or read from during rendering operations. public void Bind(int slot) Parameters slot int Which slot to use for binding. Clear() Clears the render target with the default color specified in the render target description. public void Clear() Clear(ColorF) Clears a render target with a color of your choice. This will override the default clear color specified in the render target description for this clear operation only. public void Clear(ColorF color) Parameters color ColorF

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.IShaderInputLa.summary: Class IShaderInputLayout Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Represents an instance of a shader input layout, which defines how vertex data is organized and accessed by the GPU when rendering. It encapsulates the configuration of vertex attributes, including their formats, semantic names, and input slots. The shader input layout is essential for ensuring that the vertex data is correctly interpreted by the shader programs during rendering operations. public class IShaderInputLayout : AuraResourcePointer, IDisposable Inheritance object AuraResourcePointer IShaderInputLayout Implements IDisposable Inherited Members AuraResourcePointer.Dispose() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties Hash Gets the hash code that uniquely identifies the current shader input layout configuration. public ulong Hash { get; } Property Value ulong Remarks The hash value can be used to compare shader input layouts or as a key in collections. The value is consistent for the same layout configuration but may differ across different application runs or platforms. This is cached so very fast to access. Methods GetDesc() Retrieves a description of the shader input layout associated with this object. Never make any changes to the returned description as it is the actual instance stored in the shader input layout and not a copy. public ShaderInputLayoutDesc GetDesc() Returns ShaderInputLayoutDesc A ShaderInputLayoutDesc structure that describes the current shader input layout.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.IShaderProgram.title: Class IShaderProgram | Onix Plugin Documentation
docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.IShaderProgram.summary: Class IShaderProgram Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Represents a shader, which contains the Vertex Shader, Pixel Shader and other kinds potentially. public class IShaderProgram : AuraResourcePointer, IDisposable Inheritance object AuraResourcePointer IShaderProgram Implements IDisposable Inherited Members AuraResourcePointer.Dispose() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties BytesHash Gets the hash value representing the current state of the input layout in compiled bytes. public ulong BytesHash { get; } Property Value ulong Remarks The hash can be used to efficiently compare input layouts or detect changes. The value is unique to the layout's byte representation and may change if the layout is modified. IsCompute Gets a value indicating whether the shader program is a compute shader. public bool IsCompute { get; } Property Value bool IsGlsl True when this shader is glsl. This is determined by the implementation and cannot be changed by the user. public bool IsGlsl { get; } Property Value bool IsHlsl True when this shader is hlsl of any version. This is determined by the implementation and cannot be changed by the user. public bool IsHlsl { get; } Property Value bool IsReady Gets a value indicating whether the shader program is ready for use. public bool IsReady { get; } Property Value bool Kind The kind of shader this is, like glsl, hlsl 5.1, etc. This is determined by the implementation and cannot be changed by the user. public ShaderProgramKind Kind { get; } Property Value ShaderProgramKind TextHash Gets the hash of the shader code as text. This is a 64-bit hash value that uniquely identifies the shader code based on its textual representation. The hash is computed from the shader code and can be used to compare different shader programs or to cache compiled shaders. Note that this hash may differ across different runs of the application or on different platforms, as it is based on the text of the shader code rather than its compiled binary representation. public ulong TextHash { get; } Property Value ulong Methods Compile(string, bool) Compiles the shader program using the provided shader code. If the compilation is successful, the shader program will be ready for use; otherwise, an error message will be returned. The code must have the vertex and pixel shader, named VSmain and PSmain and so on. You can also have CSmain for compute shaders, which does not require other entry points. public string? Compile(string shaderCode, bool isCompute = false) Parameters shaderCode string The code of the vertex and pixel shader, named VSmain and PSmain and so on. isCompute bool When doing a compute shader, set to true. Returns string The error message from the compilation CompileFromFile(string, bool) Compiles the shader program from a file specified by the provided file path. If the compilation is successful, the shader program will be ready for use; otherwise, an error message will be returned. The code must have the vertex and pixel shader, named VSmain and PSmain and so on. You can also have CSmain for compute shaders, which does not require other entry points. public string? CompileFromFile(string filepath, bool isCompute = false) Parameters filepath string The file path to the shader code, which should contain the vertex and pixel shader, named VSmain and PSmain and so on. isCompute bool When doing a compute shader, set to true. Returns string The error message from the compilation GetCacheBlob() Gets a binary blob that represents the compiled shader program, which can be used for caching purposes. The blob contains all the necessary information to recreate the shader program without needing to recompile the shader code. If the shader program is not ready or if there was an error during compilation, this method may return null. public byte[]? GetCacheBlob() Returns byte[] The binary cache blob or null when not available. GetRecommendedInputLayout() Gets a recommended input layout instance for this shader program. This is optional and may return null if the shader program does not provide a recommended input layout. public IShaderInputLayout? GetRecommendedInputLayout() Returns IShaderInputLayout GetRecommendedInputLayoutDesc() Gets a recommended input layout description for this shader program. Don't actually make any changes directly to this, create a copy and call SetRecommendedInputLayout(ShaderInputLayoutDesc) instead. public ShaderInputLayoutDesc GetRecommendedInputLayoutDesc() Returns ShaderInputLayoutDesc A ShaderInputLayoutDesc that describes the recommended input layout for the shader program. This is optional so it may be empty. Remarks The returned input layout is typically suitable for use when creating input layouts for vertex buffers that are intended to be used with this shader program. The exact structure of the layout depends on the shader's expected input signature. LoadFromCacheBlob(byte[]) Loads a compiled shader program from a binary cache blob. This allows you to recreate a shader program without needing to recompile the shader code, which can significantly reduce loading times. The provided cache blob should be obtained from a previous call to GetCacheBlob() for the same shader program configuration. If the cache blob is valid and compatible with the current shader program, it will be loaded successfully; otherwise, an error may occur, and the shader program may not be ready for use. public bool LoadFromCacheBlob(byte[] cacheBlob) Parameters cacheBlob byte[] The binary cache blob that represents the compiled shader program. This should be obtained from a previous call to GetCacheBlob() for the same shader program configuration. Returns bool true when the cache blob has been loaded. SetRecommendedInputLayout(ShaderInputLayoutDesc) Sets the recommended input layout for this shader program based on the shader code and its requirements. The input layout describes how vertex data should be organized and accessed by the GPU when rendering with this shader program. By setting the recommended input layout, don't have to make your own later and can tell the backend to use this one, saving you the trouble of defining it yourself. public void SetRecommendedInputLayout(ShaderInputLayoutDesc inputLayoutDesc) Parameters inputLayoutDesc ShaderInputLayoutDesc The recommended description according to you.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.ITexture.html.summary: Class ITexture Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Represents an aura texture. public class ITexture : AuraResourcePointer, IDisposable Inheritance object AuraResourcePointer ITexture Implements IDisposable Inherited Members AuraResourcePointer.Dispose() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties CanBeRendered True when the texture can be bound into a shader, for use in rendering. Clone() Clones the texture. public ITexture Clone() Returns ITexture A new ITexture instance that is a clone of this texture. CopyInto(ITexture, uint, uint) Copies a region from this texture to another texture. public void CopyInto(ITexture destination, uint srcArrayIndex = 0, uint dstArrayIndex = 0) Parameters destination ITexture The destination texture. srcArrayIndex uint Source array index. dstArrayIndex uint Destination array index. CopyTextureRegion(ITexture, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint) Copies a region from this texture to another texture. public void CopyTextureRegion(ITexture destination, uint width, uint height, uint srcX, uint srcY, uint dstX, uint dstY, uint srcArrayIndex = 0, uint dstArrayIndex = 0) Parameters destination ITexture The destination texture. width uint Width of the region. height uint Height of the region. srcX uint Source X offset. srcY uint Source Y offset. dstX uint Destination X offset. dstY uint Destination Y offset. srcArrayIndex uint Source array index. dstArrayIndex uint Destination array index. ReadbackRegion(uint, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint) Reads back a region of the texture. public byte[]? ReadbackRegion(uint x, uint y, uint width, uint height, uint arrayIndex = 0, uint mipLevel = 0) Parameters x uint X offset. y uint Y offset. width uint Width of the region. height uint Height of the region. arrayIndex uint Array index. mipLevel uint Mip level. Returns byte[] The raw pixel bytes of the region, or null if the readback failed. ReadbackRegionAsImage(uint, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint) Reads back a region of the texture as a RawImageData. Only supported for RGBA8 and BGRA8 formats; BGRA8 channels are swapped to RGBA8 automatically. public RawImageData? ReadbackRegionAsImage(uint x, uint y, uint width, uint height, uint arrayIndex = 0, uint mipLevel = 0) Parameters x uint X offset. y uint Y offset. width uint Width of the region. height uint Height of the region. arrayIndex uint Array index. mipLevel uint Mip level. Returns RawImageData A RawImageData with RGBA8 pixel data, or null if the readback failed. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when the texture format is not RGBA8 or BGRA8. ReadbackWholeTexture(uint, uint) Reads back the entire texture at the specified mip level from the GPU to CPU memory. public byte[]? ReadbackWholeTexture(uint arrayIndex = 0, uint mipLevel = 0) Parameters arrayIndex uint Array slice index for texture arrays. mipLevel uint Mip level to read from. Returns byte[] The raw pixel bytes of the mip level, or null if the readback failed. ReadbackWholeTextureAsImage(uint, uint) Reads back the entire texture at the specified mip level from the GPU as a RawImageData. Only supported for RGBA8 and BGRA8 formats; BGRA8 channels are swapped to RGBA8 automatically. public RawImageData? ReadbackWholeTextureAsImage(uint arrayIndex = 0, uint mipLevel = 0) Parameters arrayIndex uint Array slice index for texture arrays. mipLevel uint Mip level to read from. Returns RawImageData A RawImageData with RGBA8 pixel data, or null if the readback failed. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when the texture format is not RGBA8 or BGRA8. ResolveInto(ITexture) Resolves this texture into another texture. public bool ResolveInto(ITexture destination) Parameters destination ITexture The destination texture. Returns bool True if successful. UpdateTextureRegion(byte[], AuraColorFormat, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint, uint) Updates a region of the texture. Note that the width and height must match the pixel data you provide. public bool UpdateTextureRegion(byte[] data, AuraColorFormat format, uint x, uint y, uint width, uint height, uint arrayIndex = 0, uint mipLevel = 0) Parameters data byte[] The raw bitmap data to upload. format AuraColorFormat The format of the data. x uint X offset in the texture. y uint Y offset in the texture. width uint Width of the region. height uint Height of the region. arrayIndex uint Array index for texture arrays. mipLevel uint Mip level to update. Returns bool True if successful. Upload(byte[], AuraColorFormat, uint, uint) Uploads data to the texture. The data must be the entire texture x and y dimensions multiplied by the size of the format in bytes. For example, for a 256x256 RGBA8 texture, the data should be 256 * 256 * 4 = 262144 bytes. public bool Upload(byte[] data, AuraColorFormat format, uint arrayIndex = 0, uint mipLevel = 0) Parameters data byte[] The raw bitmap data to upload. Must be the size of the entire texture. format AuraColorFormat The format of the data. arrayIndex uint Array index for texture arrays. mipLevel uint Mip level to upload to. Returns bool True if successful.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.PrimitiveTopol.summary: Enum PrimitiveTopology Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Defines the topology of primitives to be rendered by the graphics pipeline. public enum PrimitiveTopology Fields LineList = 1 A list of independent line segments, where every two consecutive vertices define one line. LineStrip = 2 A continuous sequence of lines, where each new vertex connects to the previous one. PatchList = 5 A collection of control points used for tessellation shaders. PointList = 0 A list of individual points, where each vertex is drawn as a single point. TriangleList = 3 A list of independent triangles, where every three vertices define one triangle face. TriangleStrip = 4 A strip of connected triangles that share edges between consecutive triangles.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.RasterizerStat.title: Struct RasterizerStateDesc | Onix Plugin Documentation
docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.RasterizerStat.summary: Struct RasterizerStateDesc Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Describes how the rasterizer should be configured. public struct RasterizerStateDesc Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Constructors RasterizerStateDesc() Initializes a new instance of the RasterizerStateDesc struct with default settings. Back-face culling enabled, solid fill mode; all optional features disabled; depth bias zero. public RasterizerStateDesc() RasterizerStateDesc(CullMode, bool, FillMode) Initializes a new instance of the RasterizerStateDesc struct, specifying the culling and fill modes. All other properties retain default values (e.g., back-face culling, solid fill, no depth bias). public RasterizerStateDesc(CullMode cullingMode, bool enableScissors = false, FillMode fillMode = FillMode.Solid) Parameters cullingMode CullMode The primitive culling mode (None, Front, or Back). Default: Back. enableScissors bool When true, the scissor rectangles are enabled. fillMode FillMode The polygon fill mode (Solid or Wireframe). Default: Solid. Fields AntialiasedLineEnabled Enables or disables anti-aliasing for line primitives (e.g., smooth edges on lines). Note: This may not be supported on all hardware or API versions (e.g., D3D12 ignores it). public bool AntialiasedLineEnabled Field Value bool Cull Specifies which primitives are culled during rasterization. Common values include Back (default), Front, and None for no culling. public CullMode Cull Field Value CullMode DepthBias Constant depth bias added to the depth value of each rasterized pixel. Used to prevent z-fighting in shadow mapping and other techniques where geometry overlaps. Positive values push fragments away from the camera; negative pulls them closer. public float DepthBias Field Value float DepthBiasClamp Maximum clamp value for depth bias (to prevent extreme over-biasing). The actual applied bias is DepthBias + SlopeScaledDepthBias × max_slope, clamped to this range. public float DepthBiasClamp Field Value float DepthClipEnabled Enables or disables depth clipping (required for correct viewport transform and clip volume). When disabled, depth values may exceed the [0,1] range without clipping — useful for advanced techniques like inverted Z buffers or custom projection setups. public bool DepthClipEnabled Field Value bool Fill Specifies how primitives are filled during rasterization. Common values include Solid (default) for solid polygons, and Wireframe for wireframe rendering. public FillMode Fill Field Value FillMode FrontCounterClockwise Determines whether front-facing primitives have counter-clockwise vertex ordering. When true, the front face is defined by vertices in counter-clockwise order (D3D convention). Set to false for clockwise-front-face behavior (e.g., when using OpenGL-style geometry). Only effective if Cull is not None. public bool FrontCounterClockwise Field Value bool MultisampleEnabled Enables or disables multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) during rasterization. When enabled, per-sample coverage is computed; otherwise, single-sample rendering occurs. Only effective when the render target supports MSAA. public bool MultisampleEnabled Field Value bool ScissorEnabled Enables or disables the scissor test, which restricts rendering to a rectangular region. When enabled, pixels outside the configured scissor rectangle are discarded. public bool ScissorEnabled Field Value bool SlopeScaledDepthBias Depth bias scaled by the polygon's slope (e.g., steep surfaces receive greater bias). Combined with DepthBias and clamped by DepthBiasClamp. Critical for high-quality shadow maps — typically set to 0.0f or small negative values. public float SlopeScaledDepthBias Field Value float

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.SamplerDesc.Co.summary: Enum SamplerDesc.ComparisonFuncs Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Defines comparison functions for depth and stencil buffer tests. public enum SamplerDesc.ComparisonFuncs Fields Always = 8 The test always passes. Equal = 3 The test passes if the source value equals the reference value. Greater = 5 The test passes if the source value is greater than the reference value. GreaterEqual = 7 The test passes if the source value is greater than or equal to the reference value. Less = 2 The test passes if the source value is less than the reference value. LessEqual = 4 The test passes if the source value is less than or equal to the reference value. Never = 1 The test always fails. None = 0 No comparison is performed; typically disables the test. docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.html.title: Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura | Onix Plugin Documentation
docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Aura.html.summary: Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Aura Classes AuraBackendCapabilities Exposes the hardware capabilities of a graphics backend, including per-format support flags and maximum resource binding counts. Retrieve this via Capabilities. AuraBackendCapabilities.PerFormat Describes GPU support flags for a single AuraColorFormat. AuraColorFormatExtensions Extensions for the AuraColorFormat enum. AuraResourcePointer Holds an Aura resource reference. IAuraBackend The main graphics backend interface. Manages the GPU device, resource creation, pipeline state, and rendering commands. Analogous to the combination of ID3D11Device and ID3D11DeviceContext in Direct3D 11. Create one via CreateBackend(). IAuraBackendCreator Factory for creating IAuraBackend instances. Allows querying available graphics adapters and selecting an API version before creating the backend. Obtain one via the static factory methods such as CreateD3d12() or CreateD3d11(). IAuraBuffer Represents a GPU buffer resource. IAuraGraphicsAdapter Represents a physical or virtual graphics adapter (GPU) available on the system. Provides access to adapter properties such as memory sizes, hardware identifiers, and supported API versions. IAuraWindow Represents a native OS window. Provides control over window state, size, position, and appearance, as well as integration with the graphics backend for rendering. IBlendState Represents an instance of a BlendState. This dictates how blending will occur. IDepthStencilBuffer Represents a depth stencil buffer resource, containing the depth and stencil buffers depending on format. IDepthStencilState Represents an instance of a depth stencil state. This dictates how the depth buffer and stencil buffers are handled. IPipelineSnapshot A captured snapshot of the graphics pipeline state that can be restored later, useful for preserving and recovering render state around third-party hooks or interop scenarios. Obtain one via TakeSnapshot(bool, bool, bool, bool). IRasterizerState Represents an instance of a rasterizer state. This dictates how pixels are created out of geometry. IRenderTarget Represents a render target resource instance, which is a texture that can be rendered to during rendering operations. A render target allows you to draw graphics onto a texture, enabling techniques such as off-screen rendering, post-processing effects, and dynamic texture generation. ISampler Represents a texture sampler resource instance, which defines how textures are sampled during rendering operations, including filtering, addressing modes, and other sampling parameters. IShaderInputLayout Represents an instance of a shader input layout, which defines how vertex data is organized and accessed by the GPU when rendering. It encapsulates the configuration of vertex attributes, including their formats, semantic names, and input slots. The shader input layout is essential for ensuring that the vertex data is correctly interpreted by the shader programs during rendering operations. IShaderProgram Represents a shader, which contains the Vertex Shader, Pixel Shader and other kinds potentially. ITexture Represents an aura texture. ShaderInputLayoutDesc Represents a collection that describes the layout of input elements for a shader. Provides methods to define, modify, and enumerate the input elements used by a shader program. ShaderInputLayoutDesc.Storage Represents a single element in the shader input layout description. It contains the format type, semantic name, slot, and whether it's per-instance data. Structs AuraBufferDesc Describes a buffer resource, including its size, usage, and other properties that control how the buffer is created and used in graphics applications. AuraSupportedAdapterApi Describes a graphics API version supported by an IAuraGraphicsAdapter, including whether the implementation is software-based and its version identifier. BlendStateDesc Describes the blend state configuration for a set of render targets, including blending, logic operations, and color write masks. Used to control how pixel colors are combined during rendering. BlendStateDesc.BlendTarget Represents a render target blend description since all 8 render targets can have their own individual blend parameters. DepthStencilBufferDesc Describes the configuration for a depth-stencil buffer. DepthStencilStateDesc The description of the depth-stencil state, which controls how depth testing and stencil testing are performed during rendering. FullScreenDisplayMode Describes a display mode including resolution and refresh rate. Used when switching to exclusive fullscreen or querying supported modes. MsaaDesc Describes the parameters used to control multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) settings for textures, including the number of samples and quality level. RasterizerStateDesc Describes how the rasterizer should be configured. RenderTargetDesc Describes the configuration for a render target. SamplerDesc Describes the parameters used to control how textures are sampled in rendering operations, including filtering, addressing modes, level-of-detail bias, and comparison functions. TextureDesc Describes properties and configuration of a texture resource. Enums AuraColorFormat Defines pixel formats for textures, render targets, and swap chains. AuraDepthStencilFormat Defines formats for depth and stencil buffers used in rendering. AuraFormatType The type of format to use for data serialization or vertex attributes. Formats starting with 'N' mean Normalized (values are scaled between 0.0f-1.0f or -1.0f-1.0f within the entire bit length min/max). Formats starting with 'U' mean Unsigned (only positive numbers, e.g., 0 to Max). Formats starting with 'S' mean Signed (allow negative numbers, e.g., Min to Max). AuraPresentResult Represents the result of presenting a frame on a swap chain. That's usually where you'll be alerted of any major error. AuraSamplerAddressMode Defines how texture coordinates outside the [0,1] range are handled during sampling. AuraSamplerFilterType Defines the filtering mode used when sampling a texture. BlendLogicOperation Defines logic operations for pixel blending using bitwise boolean calculations. BlendOperation Defines the operation used to combine source and destination colors/alphas during blending. BlendType Defines blending factors used in the pixel shader output merger stage. BufferBindUsage Defines the usage flags for binding buffer resources to the graphics pipeline. CullMode Defines which faces of a primitive are culled during rasterization. FillMode Defines how the interior of primitives is rasterized. FullScreenState Defines the fullscreen state of a window. PrimitiveTopology Defines the topology of primitives to be rendered by the graphics pipeline. SamplerDesc.ComparisonFuncs Defines comparison functions for depth and stencil buffer tests. ShaderProgramKind Defines the shader language and profile version used for compiling graphics programs. StencilComparisonFunc Defines comparison functions for stencil buffer testing. StencilOperation Defines operations applied to the stencil buffer value during rendering.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Entities.EntityAttr.title: Enum EntityAttributeId | Onix Plugin Documentation
docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Entities.EntityAttr.summary: Enum EntityAttributeId Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Entities Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Identifiers for entity attributes. public enum EntityAttributeId Fields Absorption = 14 This is the yellow hearts the Absorption effect grants. AttackDamage = 13 The attack damage. How much damage can the entity deal? Exhaustion = 3 The exhaustion. Not too sure what this one does, feel free to inform me so I can update this documentation. Experience = 5 The current experience points of the player for that level. FollowRange = 8 The follow range. How far will the entity follow its target? Health = 7 The current health of the player. Hunger = 1 The hunger. Remember, you're not yourself when you're hungry. JumpStrength = 16 The jump strength. I think this is only ever used for horses, but maybe not. KnockbackResistance = 9 The knockback resistance. How resistant is the entity to knockback? LavaMovementSpeed = 12 The lava movement speed. How fast can the entity move in lava? Level = 4 The current level of the player. Luck = 15 99% of gamblers quit before hitting it big. MovementSpeed = 10 The movement speed. How fast can the entity move? Saturation = 2 The saturation. Basically hunger but invisible. UnderwaterMovementSpeed = 11 The underwater movement speed. How fast can the entity move underwater?

SendPluginMessage(string, string) Sends a plugin message with the specified message ID and content to the player. If the player has their PluginConnectionEstablished property set to true, the message will be sent. The messageId parameter only has to be unique in your plugin as your plugin's uuid and version are also gathered for you to make them unique. You can use one of the global event variant to handle another plugin's messages (or a different version if you plan on perfect backwards compatibility for some reason or want to give the user an error). public void SendPluginMessage(string messageId, string message) Parameters messageId string The Id that will be used for you to identify what the content might be. message string The message content as a string.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Entities.html.summary: Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Entities Classes Entity Represents an entity in the world. For dropped items. LocalPlayer Represents the local player in the game. Mob Represents a mob entity, providing access to mob-specific properties and inventory handling. MobEffectIdExtensions Extension methods for MobEffectId, including conversion and icon retrieval. MobEffectInstance Represents an instance of a mob effect applied to an entity, including its properties and duration. MutableEntityAttribute Represents a mutable entity attribute, allowing modification of its value and limits. Player Represents a player entity, providing access to player-specific properties and inventory handling. PlayerMovementInputs Represents the player's current input state. PlayerSkin Represents a Minecraft player skin, including geometry, images, and metadata. ServerConnectedPlayer Represents a player connected to the server, including platform, identity, and skin information. ServerPlayer Represents a server-side player entity, providing server-specific player functionality. Enums CommandPermissionLevel Represents the command permission level of a player. EntityAttributeId Identifiers for entity attributes. EntityCategory Specifies the category or categories that an entity can belong to. EntityFlag Flags representing various states and properties that an entity can have. GameBuildPlatform Represents the build platform of a connected game client. GameMode Represents the game mode of a player. MobEffectId Identifiers for all possible mob effects. PlayerPermissionLevel Represents the player permission level. PlayerSkin.ArmSizeType Specifies the arm size type for a player skin. PlayerSkinTrust Indicates the trust level of a player skin.

If you want to keep the block, use region's GetBlock(BlockPos) at position. You can also use the runtime ID and the GetBlockFromRuntimeId(uint) for both old or new block if you want to keep it. public delegate void OnixEventLocalServerWorld.OnBlockChangedDelegate(WorldBlocks region, BlockPos position, Block oldBlock, Block newBlock, int layer, WorldBlocks.BlockUpdateType updateType) Parameters region WorldBlocks The WorldBlocks that did the change./// position BlockPos The BlockPos of the block that was modified. oldBlock Block The Block instance that previously occupied the position. Don't keep this. newBlock Block The Block instance that replaced the old block. Don't keep this. layer int The layer, there are two layers. 0 is the main layer, 1 is generally used for waterlogging and things snow layers merging with some plants. updateType WorldBlocks.BlockUpdateType A WorldBlocks.BlockUpdateType flag that specifies how the update should be handled, such as updating neighbors, notifying the network, skipping graphics updates, or forcing priority updates.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Events.OnixEventRen.summary: Delegate OnixEventRendering.LowLevelAuraRenderDelegate Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Events Assembly OnixRuntime.dll This is very low level, not for the weak. This is a D3D11 like API for graphics. This wrapper supports DirectX 12 and 11. You should look at the aura example plugin and ideally know some D3D11. You start in a BeginFrame(bool) context and should exit the callback in such a way. Depending on what you do, you might need to restore the pipeline to a workable starting point. You should never keep the backend, and you need to dispose of every reference to the back buffer render target, which is going to be the game's. public delegate void OnixEventRendering.LowLevelAuraRenderDelegate(IAuraBackend backend, float deltaTime, string screenName, bool isHudHidden, bool isClientUI) Parameters backend IAuraBackend The aura backend for the game. You are in a frame that has been BeginFrame(bool) and must be at the exit too. deltaTime float The amount of seconds since the last frame, clamped between 0.001f to 1.0f. screenName string The name of the top screen the game is on. isHudHidden bool True when the hud is hidden with F1. isClientUI bool True when in a client UI that is not the hud screen.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Events.OnixEventSch.title: Class OnixEventScheduler | Onix Plugin Documentation
docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Events.OnixEventSch.summary: Class OnixEventScheduler Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Events Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Manages execution context switching for asynchronous operations to ensure code runs on the correct game thread or tick. public class OnixEventScheduler Inheritance object OnixEventScheduler Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks This scheduler allows developers to sequence async logic that hops between background threads and specific game loops (e.g., Main Tick, Server Tick, or Render loops). Key features include: Context Switching: Awaitable methods to pause execution until the next specific game event occurs. Fire-and-Forget Handling: Use HandleTask(Task) to execute tasks without blocking, ensuring exceptions are logged rather than crashing the application. Game Utilities: Integrated helpers for managing inventory state and awaiting vanilla command responses. Methods ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse(string, CancellationToken) Executes a game command asynchronously and waits for the result to come in. This only works for commands that return a proper response. Some servers use text packets instead for command output, making this function not work. But on a server that implemented commands responsibly, this is a great way to run a command and get the result of specifically that command in a split way. Uses a timeout of 20 seconds by default, which should be more than enough for any command to respond. If the timeout is reached without receiving a response, this function will return null. public Task<VanillaCommandResponse?> ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse(string command, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters command string The command to run. ct CancellationToken A cancellation token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<VanillaCommandResponse> A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the command response, or null if the timeout is reached. Examples var testforCommandRes = await Scheduler.ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse("/testfor @e[rm=1]"); if (testforCommandRes is not null) { Console.WriteLine($"There are {testforCommandRes.SuccessCount} entities around you."); Console.WriteLine("They are: " + string.Join(", ", testforCommandRes.Messages .Where(x => x.MessageParams.Length > 0) .Select(x => x.MessageParams.LastOrDefault("")))); testforCommandRes.ShouldSilence = true; } Exceptions OperationCanceledException Whenever the cancellation token is canceled, but not when the timeout expires. ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse(string, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) Executes a game command asynchronously and waits for the result to come in. This only works for commands that return a proper response. Some servers use text packets instead for command output, making this function not work. But on a server that implemented commands responsibly, this is a great way to run a command and get the result of specifically that command in a split way. public Task<VanillaCommandResponse?> ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse(string command, TimeSpan timeout, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters command string The command to run. timeout TimeSpan The maximum amount of time to wait for a response. After that time, this function will return null. ct CancellationToken A cancellation token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<VanillaCommandResponse> A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the command response, or null if the timeout is reached. Examples var testforCommandRes = await Scheduler.ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse("/testfor @e[rm=1]", TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)); if (testforCommandRes is not null) { Console.WriteLine($"There are {testforCommandRes.SuccessCount} entities around you."); Console.WriteLine("They are: " + string.Join(", ", testforCommandRes.Messages .Where(x => x.MessageParams.Length > 0) .Select(x => x.MessageParams.LastOrDefault("")))); testforCommandRes.ShouldSilence = true; } Exceptions OperationCanceledException Whenever the cancellation token is canceled, but not when the timeout expires. ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponseCallback(string, Action<VanillaCommandResponse?>, CancellationToken) Executes a game command and waits for the result to come in. This only works for commands that return a proper response. Some servers use text packets instead for command output, making this function not work. But on a server that implemented commands responsibly, this is a great way to run a command and get the result of specifically that command in a split way. docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Events.html.title: Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Events | Onix Plugin Documentation
docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Events.html.summary: Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Events Classes OnixEventAudio Provides events for client audio related things. OnixEventCommon Provides common event hooks for tick, rendering, input, and chat message events. OnixEventGame Provides game-related events (URI invocations, etc.). OnixEventGui Provides events for GUI screens such as container screens and chat screens. OnixEventInputs Provides events for input actions, analog movement, player input ticks, text input, and input reset. OnixEventLocalServerWorld The class hosting the local server events. OnixEventPlayer Provides events for local player actions such as breaking, building, using items, and interacting with entities. OnixEventRendering Provides rendering-related events (world, HUD, screen rendering, 2D/Direct2D hooks). Subscribe to the events to receive renderer objects and timing deltas. Handlers are invoked with an appropriate renderer instance depending on the current rendering backend. OnixEventScheduler Manages execution context switching for asynchronous operations to ensure code runs on the correct game thread or tick. OnixEventWorld Provides events for handling world-related actions. OnixEvents Root container for all Onix event groups. Provides typed access to each domain of events (session, rendering, input, GUI, game, etc.). Instantiate once and subscribe to the specific event group(s) you need. OnixEventsSession Provides events for session tick, join, leave, and game pause/resume. Delegates OnixEventAudio.OnSoundPlayedInUiDelegate Called when a sound is played in the UI. OnixEventAudio.OnSoundPlayedInWorldDelegate Called when a sound is played in the world. OnixEventGame.OnUriInvokedDelegate Called when a URI is invoked. specific to plugins. Not logic safe. The plugin uri that was invoked, the format goes as follows. minecraft://plugin.onixclient.com/{verb}?{key}={value}&{myKey}={myValue} You should use this whenever possible to make it clear it's for plugins and avoid conflicts if you're implementing custom ones. OnixEventGame.OnUriInvokedRawDelegate The raw uri that was invoked e.g. "minecraft://openServersTab" When implementing your own uri handlers you should use UriInvoked. OnixEventGui.OnChatScreenTabCompleteDelegate Delegate for handling chat screen tab completion events. OnixEventGui.OnChatScreenTickDelegate Delegate for handling chat screen tick events. OnixEventGui.OnContainerScreenHoverTextRequestedDelegate Represents a method that is called to retrieve the hover text for a container screen when an item is hovered over. You can change or replace the text however you want, return the text that will be shown to the user. If you have no changes to make, you should return text DO NOT USE GetHoverText(RuntimeWorld, bool, bool) or GetHoverText(bool, bool) unless you set vanilla to true. Otherwise, you will get infinite recursion. OnixEventGui.OnContainerScreenTickDelegate Delegate for handling container screen tick events. OnixEventInputs.OnInputDelegate Delegate for handling input events (keyboard, mouse, etc.). OnixEventInputs.OnInputResetDelegate Delegate for handling input reset events. OnixEventInputs.OnPlayerInputTickDelegate Delegate for handling player input tick events. OnixEventInputs.OnRawTextCharDelegate Delegate for handling raw text character input events. OnixEventInputs.OnShouldCancelAnalogMovementDelegate Delegate for handling analog movement cancellation events. OnixEventInputs.OnTextCharDelegate Delegate for handling text character input events. OnixEventLocalServerWorld.OnAreaChangedDelegate Delegate that is invoked whenever an area in the world changes. OnixEventLocalServerWorld.OnBlockChangedDelegate Delegate that is invoked whenever a block in the world changes. Provides context about the region, position, old and new blocks, as well as how the change should be propagated and rendered. If you want to keep the block, use region's GetBlock(BlockPos) at position. You can also use the runtime ID and the GetBlockFromRuntimeId(uint) for both old or new block if you want to keep it. OnixEventLocalServerWorld.OnPlayerJoinedDelegate Delegate that is invoked whenever a player joins the local server. This is a server only event, so only when you are hosting the world. The player may show up in the entity list before this event is fired, but this event should be fired when the player is ready to rock and roll. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerAttackDelegate Delegate for handling when a player attacks an entity. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerBreakBlockDelegate Delegate for handling when a player breaks a block. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerBuildBlockDelegate Delegate for handling when a player builds a block. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerInteractDelegate Delegate for handling when a player interacts with an entity. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerStartBreakBlockDelegate Delegate for handling when a player starts breaking a block. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerStopUsingItemDelegate Delegate for handling when a player stops using an item. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerUseItemDelegate Delegate for handling when a player uses an item. OnixEventPlayer.OnLocalServerPlayerUseItemOnDelegate Delegate for handling when a player uses an item on a block. OnixEventRendering.LowLevelAuraRenderDelegate This is very low level, not for the weak. This is a D3D11 like API for graphics. This wrapper supports DirectX 12 and 11. You should look at the aura example plugin and ideally know some D3D11. You start in a BeginFrame(bool) context and should exit the callback in such a way. Depending on what you do, you might need to restore the pipeline to a workable starting point. You should never keep the backend, and you need to dispose of every reference to the back buffer render target, which is going to be the game's. OnixEventRendering.OnAuraDeviceLostDelegate Delegate for handling graphics device loss events. OnixEventRendering.OnHudRender2DDelegate This event is called when on hud, hide hud is false and there is no client UI screen opened. This will be called from the user's preferred 2D renderer. This may or may not be a logic callback so don't access game state, entities, etc. OnixEventRendering.OnHudRenderDelegate Called when HUD should be rendered via the game's renderer. Logic-safe: game state and entities are available. OnixEventRendering.OnPreRenderScreenDelegate Delegate for the game's rendering callbacks (always logic-safe). OnixEventRendering.OnPreRenderScreenDirect2DDelegate This event is called all the time. The Pre is before the client's screens are rendered, not the game's. You should avoid this if RenderHudDirect2D gives you what you need. debug_screen should always be there if you want to pick that one, otherwise you can ignore debug_screen and toast_screen to have just the main screen. This will never be a logic callback so don't access game state, entities, etc. OnixEventRendering.OnRenderHudDirect2DDelegate This event is called when on hud, hide hud is false and there is no client UI screen opened. This will be called from the user's preferred 2D renderer. This will never be a logic callback so don't access game state, entities, etc. OnixEventRendering.OnRenderScreen2DDelegate This event is called all the time. You should avoid this if HudRender gives you what you need. This will be called from the user's preferred 2D renderer. This may or may not be a logic callback so don't access game state, entities, etc. There is no PreRenderScreen2D event, because depending on the renderer, pre means different things. You can handle this case manually by checking the different pre events and MainRenderer. OnixEventRendering.OnRenderScreenDelegate This event is called all the time. (always logic-safe) This is a logic callback so you can access game state, entities, etc. OnixEventRendering.OnRenderScreenDirect2DDelegate This event is called all the time. You should avoid this if RenderHudDirect2D gives you what you need. This will never be a logic callback so don't access game state, entities, etc. OnixEventRendering.OnWorldRenderDelegate Called when the world (3D) should be rendered. Logic-safe: game state and entities are available. OnixEventRendering.ShouldHideScreenDelegate This is only for game screens, returning true will prevent that screen from rendering. Delegate used to determine whether a given game screen should be hidden. Return true to prevent rendering of that screen. OnixEventWorld.OnAreaChangedDelegate Delegate that is invoked whenever an area in the world changes. OnixEventWorld.OnBlockChangedDelegate Delegate that is invoked whenever a block in the world changes. Provides context about the region, position, old and new blocks, as well as how the change should be propagated and rendered. OnixEventsSession.OnDimensionChangedDelegate Delegate for handling dimension change events. OnixEventsSession.OnSessionJoinedDelegate Delegate for handling join events. OnixEventsSession.OnSessionLeftDelegate Delegate for handling leave events. OnixEventsSession.OnTickDelegate Delegate for handling game tick events.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Internal.SharedMemo.summary: Enum SharedMemoryAddressContainer.PointerType Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Internal Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Represents a shared memory address pointer for passing and owning shared memory with an unmanaged context. public enum SharedMemoryAddressContainer.PointerType Fields Disposed = 4 The object has been disposed. You can no longer use it. Raw = 2 Just a raw pointer, YOLO! Shared = 0 A shared pointer reference. You share real ownership with others, or maybe you're the last thing keeping it alive. This object will not disappear until all references are released. Unique = 3 You own that object, it's all yours. You own it. Once you're done with it it's joever for it. Weak = 1 A weak reference to the object. This object might disappear leaving you lost and confused.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.Maths.Transformatio.summary: Enum TransformationMatrix.PerspectiveHandedness Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.Maths Assembly OnixRuntime.dll Specifies the handedness and depth range conventions for perspective matrices. public enum TransformationMatrix.PerspectiveHandedness Fields Default = 0 Whatever the default is for glm right now. Left = 1 Whatever the default left handed matrix is for glm right now. Left_NegativeOneToOne = 3 Right handed with a depth range of -1 to 1 like OpenGL. Left_ZeroToOne = 2 Left handed with a depth range of 0 to 1 like Direct3D and Vulkan. This is what you'd want to use when speaking to the game. Right = 4 Whatever the default right handed matrix is for glm right now. Right_NegativeOneToOne = 6 Right handed with a depth range of -1 to 1 like OpenGL. Right_ZeroToOne = 5 Right handed with a depth range of 0 to 1 like Direct3D and Vulkan. This is what you'd want to use when speaking to the game. Remarks This enumeration defines various combinations of handedness (left-handed or right-handed) and depth range conventions used in 3D graphics. These conventions are commonly used in graphics APIs such as Direct3D, Vulkan, and OpenGL. The values in this enumeration allow developers to specify the desired matrix convention for rendering or interacting with graphics systems.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands.summary: Enum CommandExecutionTarget Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands Assembly OnixRuntime.dll This defines what side(s) the command can be executed on. If you do a command for both, it will work with both /. and . but be careful or full of care to not guess the side and check the origin. Or get your base types from the origin too, that's cool too. [Flags] public enum CommandExecutionTarget Fields Any = Both | OutOfWorld Be careful, there is a chance you would rather want Both. This can run in the menu and anywhere else, which means no one ran the command, no world info to get or anything. Both = Client | Server The command works on both client and server, it will work with both /. and . Make sure to get everything you need from the origin and not assume anything. Client = 1 The command is a client command, it will work with . OutOfWorld = 4 The command can be executed in the menu or really absolutely anywhere. Server = 2 The command is a server command, it will work with /.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands.summary: Enum CommandParameterType Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands Assembly OnixRuntime.dll The various types of command parameters that can be parsed. public enum CommandParameterType Fields Angles = 14 A pair of angles, yaw and pitch. Yaw is left-right and pitch is up-down. Angles. Angles3 = 15 A triplet of angles, yaw and pitch and roll. Yaw is left-right and pitch is up-down and roll well, you flip it around.. Angles3. Block = 16 A Block that is registered in this session. BlockPos = 11 A single integer block position, supports relative (~). BlockPos. Bool = 1 Just true or false, it's not that deep... CommandPath = 0 This is used for sub commands, it's kind of like an enum but just one option will work. Entities = 9 Targets multiple entities with a selector. Entity. Entity = 8 This is any entity, it must be loaded for it to resolve. This is not too useful because it can be quite annoying to target a single entity. Entity. EntitySelector = 10 This is a selector that can target entities, players, the command source (self) and more. It supports most selector options. CommandEntitySelector. Enum = 20 This forces the user to chose between a few options. All you have to do is define your enum and have it in your commmand overload as a parameter. If you want to add icons or change the text that shows up in the auto-complete, you can use CommandEnumNameAttribute and CommandEnumIconAttribute on the enum members. Float = 3 Any floating point number, like 0.5 or -3.14 Int = 2 Any number from int.MinValue to int.MaxValue Item = 17 An Item that is registered in this session. ItemStack = 18 An ItemStack without a count but having data and optional NBT data. Format: item,data{NBT} where only item is required. If you want count, add an int for it after the item, then you can just set Count. Nbt = 19 This parses nbt text into an ObjectTag or an ArrayListTag. It must start with a { and end with a } or a [ and a ]. If you want to support both, make your parameter an NbtTag and check which you got! Player = 6 This is a player entity, it must be loaded for it to resolve. Don't use this just for a name. Player. Players = 7 This is a list of player entities, this lets the user select multiple players with selectors. Player. Position = 12 A single floating-point position, supports relative (~). Vec3. RawString = 5 This will dump everything remaining in the command as a single string, it does not support escape sequences or quotes. You can use the OnixCommandBase.RawStringAttribute on a string parameter to turn it into a raw string. SoftEnum = 21 This gives suggestions to the user in the auto complete without enforcing. You can still have icons. This one you must register and maintain elsewhere in your code using. CommandEnumRegistry's RegisterSoftEnum methods. String = 4 Some text, can be multiple words if quoted with "", it supports escape sequences like \n, \t, \r and " Vec2 = 13 X and Y coordinates. Does not support lcoal or relative as it wouldn't know relative to what. Vec2.

docs/OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands.summary: Namespace OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands Classes CommandBlockPosition Represents a block position that can be absolute or relative. CommandEntitySelector Represents a command selector. CommandEntitySelector.InvertableFilter<T> Stores a value with a flag to know if it's inverted or not. CommandEnumIconAttribute This lets you add an icon to your enum's value in the intellisense. CommandEnumNameAttribute This lets you change the name the user needs to type for that value. By default, it will convert the names to snake_case. CommandEnumRegistry This is a registry for command enums, it lets you hold enum values, their icons, change and register them. This is what you use to make them available for command arguments of type enum. Soft enums are suggested values that can be added to at runtime, they don't have to be predefined and the user doesn't have to put one of those values. Enums are values that are predefined (you can change them later by re-registering the enum) and the user has to pick one of those values, nothing else. CommandEnumRegistry.EnumValue The value type for enums, having the icon and the actual int value. CommandEnumRegistry.SoftEnumValue The value type for a soft enum, having the icon and the actual value string. CommandEnumTypeNameAttribute You should probably not use this but if you do then fair enough I guess. This is to have the parser link the original enum type name to this parameter. CommandNbtTagTypeAttribute Metadata for the parser to know what types to allow. CommandOverload Represents a specific overload of a command, defining its parameters and their types. CommandParserMetadataAttribute This is an attribute that will be given to the parser as metadata. This is essentially a base attribute type that tells it what to collect. CommandPathAttribute This lets you attach a path to a parameter, specifically a string. It's kind of like an enum, but the command can only execute if the name matches. This is useful for subcommands. This goes on a string and will always contain the path's name in the parameter as it's the only option that will be allowed to be called. Different overloads can have different path values, keeping only the ones that match the input. See the command guide if it's still unclear, basically it's selecting one value of an 'enum', not any others. CommandPosition Represents a position that can be absolute or relative. OnixCommandBase The base class for all commands. You should inherit from this class to create your own commands. You should mark overload methods with the OnixCommandBase.OverloadAttribute attribute for them to be called. OnixCommandBase.OverloadAttribute This is the attribute you need to put on your function for it to be considered. OnixCommandBase.RawStringAttribute This marks this string parameter as a raw string. This must be the last parameter, it will eat the whole input. (it was hungry.) OnixCommandBase.SoftEnumNameAttribute This lets you attach a soft enum to a string parameter. OnixCommandOrigin Wraper around the origin of a command getting run. When you check IsInWorld, you can assume World, Dimension and Region are not null. When you check IsEntity, you can assume Entity, World, Dimension and Region are not null. When you check IsClientSide, you can run client specific code. OnixCommandOutput Represents the output of a command execution. OnixCommandParameter Represents a parameter for an onix command. OnixCommandRegistry This class manages the registration and unregistration of commands for both client and server. RemoteServerCommand Represents a command that the server has. This command is there for intellisense purposes only. Enums CommandEntitySelector.SelectionOrder The order in which to select entities. The following are not supported, by lack of information or for scores, lazyness. scores=, tag=, has_property=, hasitem=, haspermission= CommandEntitySelector.SelectorType The type of selector. CommandExecutionTarget This defines what side(s) the command can be executed on. If you do a command for both, it will work with both /. and . but be careful or full of care to not guess the side and check the origin. Or get your base types from the origin too, that's cool too. CommandParameterType The various types of command parameters that can be parsed.
